questions.q: What is BigQuery's current SQL dialect called, replacing its older legacy dialect?
options: Standard SQL
BigQuery Classic SQL
GoogleSQL Legacy
ANSI BigQuery
questions.explain: Google's current BigQuery dialect is called Standard SQL, distinct from the older, now-legacy SQL dialect BigQuery originally shipped with.

questions.q: What does a fully-qualified BigQuery table name typically look like?
options: Backtick-quoted, spanning project, dataset, and table, e.g. `project.dataset.table`
Bracket-quoted, like T-SQL's [schema].[table]
Double-quoted with only a schema and table, no project
BigQuery does not support fully-qualified table names
questions.explain: BigQuery's distinctive visual signature is a backtick-quoted three-part name covering project, dataset, and table.

questions.q: Which platform in this course is closest in syntax to PostgreSQL?
options: Redshift, because it's built on an older fork of Postgres
BigQuery, because it uses Standard SQL
Snowflake, because it's also ANSI-heavy
Databricks SQL, because of its Spark heritage
questions.explain: Amazon Redshift is PostgreSQL-derived, making its syntax closer to PostgreSQL than any other platform covered in this course.

questions.q: What do Redshift's DISTKEY and SORTKEY control?
options: How data is physically distributed across compute nodes and ordered on disk
Which columns are allowed to be NULL
Which users can query a given table
The default character set for string columns
questions.explain: DISTKEY and SORTKEY are Redshift-specific DDL controlling physical data distribution across nodes and on-disk ordering — a physical-design concern.

questions.q: Why are Redshift's DISTKEY/SORTKEY concepts out of scope for this course?
options: They're an administration/physical-design concern, not part of the SQL language comparison this course focuses on
Because Redshift is deprecated and no longer used
Because they don't actually exist in real Redshift syntax
Because they are identical to T-SQL's indexing syntax and need no separate coverage
questions.explain: This course's scope is the SQL language itself; DISTKEY/SORTKEY are real Redshift syntax but belong to administration and physical table design, not language comparison.
